question: What is the primary focus of health maintenance?
explanation: Health maintenance aims to keep people well and stop diseases before they start rather than just reacting to sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why does community health nursing place a strong emphasis on health maintenance?

options.A: It completely eliminates all infectious diseases from a population
options.B: It shifts the nurse's job entirely to administrative desk work
options.C: It makes physical examinations completely unnecessary for adults
options.D: It reduces the need for expensive hospital care by stopping illness early

explanation: Focusing on wellness helps catch problems early and keeps people out of hospital beds. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which nursing action is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Checking blood pressure at a community health fair
options.B: Teaching foot care to a patient with diabetes
options.C: Providing cardiac rehabilitation after a heart attack
options.D: Administering a routine measles vaccine to a child

explanation: Vaccines stop a disease from occurring in the first place, which is the definition of primary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h2)

question: A nurse organizes a community screening program to check blood sugar levels in adults over forty. Which level of prevention does this represent?
explanation: Screenings are designed to find hidden health problems early so treatment can start right away, which is secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is a primary focus of health assessment in older adults?

options.B: Evaluating cognitive function and fall risks
options.C: Checking birth weight and Apgar scores

explanation: Older adults face unique age-related challenges like memory changes and balance issues that require targeted assessments. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why must nurses alter health assessments across different life stages?

options.A: Hospital policies require a different form for every single year of life
options.B: Medical equipment only works properly on elderly patients
options.C: Adults do not need physical examinations like children do
options.D: Different age groups face distinct health risks and developmental needs

explanation: A newborn needs different checks than a teenager or an older adult because their bodies and life risks change over time. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h3)

question: How do vaccines primarily protect the human body against infectious diseases?

options.A: By lowering body temperature during an active viral infection
options.B: By destroying bacteria directly with heavy doses of antibiotics
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to produce protective antibodies
options.D: By cleaning harmful toxins directly out of the bloodstream

explanation: Vaccines teach the immune system to recognize and fight off specific germs safely. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of achieving high community vaccination coverage?

options.A: Ensuring pharmaceutical companies sell enough medication each year
options.B: Preventing chronic non-communicable illnesses like diabetes
options.C: Creating herd immunity to protect vulnerable people who cannot be vaccinated
options.D: Eliminating the need for any handwashing or sanitation practices

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, germs have a hard time spreading, which keeps fragile individuals safe. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h4)

question: What should a nurse do first when planning health education for a patient from a different cultural background?

options.A: Insist that the patient follow hospital routines strictly at home
options.B: Hand out standard English brochures without discussing them
options.C: Assume the patient already knows basic community health rules
options.D: Assess the patient's language, literacy level, and cultural beliefs

explanation: Education only works if the nurse understands how the patient communicates and what they believe about health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is active listening an important skill in health promotion?

options.A: It helps the nurse uncover barriers stopping the patient from being healthy
options.B: It replaces the need to check vital signs or physical health
options.C: It shortens the time required for documentation paperwork
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never develop a chronic illness

explanation: Listening carefully lets nurses find out if fear, cost, or confusion is getting in the way of a patient's care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical focus of occupational health nursing?

options.A: Managing pediatric developmental milestones in schools
options.B: Promoting the use of proper personal protective equipment
options.C: Inspecting work areas for ergonomic strain and safety risks
options.D: Identifying workplace hazards like toxic chemicals

explanation: Occupational health deals specifically with worker safety and workplace hazards, not school-aged child development. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why must community nurses pay close attention to environmental conditions like water and air quality?

options.A: Environmental hazards can cause widespread illness in the community
options.B: Water and air quality have no direct connection to human wellbeing
options.C: Monitoring the environment is solely the job of local police officers
options.D: Clean air and water are only important inside hospital buildings

explanation: Polluted water or air directly exposes entire populations to toxins and infectious disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating a community health program?

options.A: To punish staff members who failed to meet performance targets
options.B: To determine if the program met its goals and improved health outcomes
options.C: To increase the cost of healthcare services for local residents
options.D: To make sure no documentation paperwork is ever filed twice

explanation: Evaluation lets nurses see if their efforts actually helped the community or if changes are needed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h7)

question: A nurse reviews attendance records and participant feedback after a nutrition workshop. What phase of the nursing process for community programs does this represent?
explanation: Reviewing records and gathering feedback after a program is finished is part of evaluating its success. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h7)
